source_name: ENER — Unique National Electronic Registry of Regulations
why_relevant: Mandatory pre-adoption publication point for draft laws and regulatory impact assessments, with a 30-day public-comment window. This is where a payments/fiscalisation bill becomes visible months before the Official Gazette — the single best early-warning source for the cell, and it also exposes the stakeholder comments filed by banks and vendors.

source_name: Official Gazette of the Republic of North Macedonia (Службен весник)
why_relevant: Legal record of enactment: laws, bylaws (правилници) and decisions take effect on publication here. Authoritative for the exact text and in-force date of payment-services, fiscalisation and e-invoicing rules, and for the secondary regulation that carries the technical requirements.

source_name: Assembly (Собрание) of the Republic of North Macedonia — materials and enacted-laws list
why_relevant: Parliamentary stage of the legislative pipeline: submitted bills, committee materials, amendments and the running list of adopted laws. Bridges the gap between ENER (draft) and Службен весник (enacted) and shows amendments made in passage.

Catalogue of datasets published by ministries and agencies (reported as 280+ datasets from 50+ institutions, CSV/JSON). Serves as a pointer to machine-readable MoF/UJP/ДЗС releases that are otherwise buried as PDFs, and reveals which institutions publish structured data at all.

source_name: Ministry of Digital Transformation (Министерство за дигитална трансформација, МДТ) — portal and post-body file store
why_relevant: Adjacent state actor whose draft laws (published on ENER as part of the EU Reform Agenda) govern e-identity, e-services and digital infrastructure that e-invoicing and digital payments ride on. Its portal.mdt.gov.mk file store also republishes MoF documents (e.g. the payment-services law text and public-debt strategy), sometimes more fetchable than finance.gov.mk itself.

source_name: Government of RNM (Влада) — sessions, decisions and government portal
why_relevant: Cabinet is the formal proposer of MoF bills and adopter of national strategies. Session conclusions and press material date-stamp when a payments/fiscalisation bill was approved for parliament, and the site indexes ministry pages and open-government commitments.

source_name: Ogledalo na Vladata (Огледало на Владата) — regulations/transparency monitor
why_relevant: Civil-society monitor that indexes and critiques government regulation-making and ENER compliance. Useful as an independent pointer to regulations that were adopted with skipped consultation, and as a cross-check on official transparency claims.

source_name: Pravdiko.mk — legal-analysis portal on MK financial and fiscal law
why_relevant: Practitioner legal portal that explains fiscalisation thresholds, cash-register obligations and financial-law amendments in plain Macedonian, usually citing the Official Gazette number. Fast triage layer that tells you which gazette issue to pull.

Business-press coverage that repeatedly breaks MoF legislative intent ahead of formal publication (e.g. planned amendments to the Banking Law and the FX Operations Law; e-invoicing impact on firms). Useful early-warning and interpretation layer for state policy.

source_name: Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems (ЗПУПС) — consolidated text and explanatory materials
why_relevant: The MoF-drafted PSD2-style law (in force from 20 April 2022; market opening for new payment service providers and e-money issuers from 1 January 2023) is the legal anchor for the entire MK payments-competition question. This government-hosted PDF and the NBRM presentation of the same law are the accessible full texts.

Systematically converts bank quarterly/semi-annual filings into readable stories (profit deltas, deposit volumes) and covers supervisory-board / management appointments. Has an archive domain (arhiva.emagazin.mk) giving multi-year back-history for trend work.
Historic archive of the same outlet — useful for reconstructing multi-year timelines of bank CEO changes and fee/tariff news that the live site no longer surfaces.

Mainstream business daily-portal with a dedicated finance desk; covers bank results, fintech/payments launches (e.g. IutePay initiatives) and regulator statements. High publishing cadence makes it a good early-signal tripwire.

Long-running MK business magazine publishing analyses and interviews with bankers/regulators — the interview format often surfaces strategy statements (branch/digital plans, card economics) absent from formal disclosures.

First private MK news agency; its economy desk reliably carries National Bank decisions (e.g. countercyclical capital buffer rate) and macro-projection stories the same day, giving a wire-speed mirror of regulator communications.

Broke detailed consumer-facing coverage of banks' new tariff books (bill-payment fee moving 90→120 MKD, mortgage commissions). Tariff/fee changes are exactly the payments-pricing signal rarely announced as a press release.

Runs computational stories off bank filings — e.g. how much domestic banks earned from fees and commissions — which is precisely the payments-revenue metric of interest and is not published in that form officially.

Consumer-advocacy/investigative outlet; covered the Komercijalna Banka card-service outage and its restoration. Best-positioned MK source for customer complaints, service failures and disputes that banks do not disclose.

Daily newspaper (published in MK and reportedly EN) that covers quarterly bank results in euro-denominated framing useful for cross-country comparison; adds a second independent confirmation layer for earnings signals.

High-traffic general portal that covered e-money licensing (Flex Pay obtaining a National Bank electronic-money licence) — licensing events are a leading indicator of new payments entrants and are otherwise buried in regulator registers.
Carries video/interview reactions from consumer-side commentators on bank fee increases (e.g. Krmov on 120-denar payment commissions), capturing the advocacy/complaint side of payments pricing.
Business-news site covering money flows relevant to payments volumes (e.g. remittances/дознаки driving the market) — a demand-side context source for card and transfer business.

The dominant MK news aggregator: clusters the same story across dozens of outlets, so it is the cheapest way to (a) discover MK outlets not yet on our list and (b) detect the moment a bank signal goes multi-outlet. Its section index (time.mk/s/) is effectively a directory of MK media.
Second aggregator; indexed the Komercijalna Banka service-outage story. Useful redundancy against TIME.mk and a different outlet mix.

source_name: GRID.mk — aggregator of MK portals and TV
why_relevant: Aggregates MK portals plus television output; historically indexed Komercijalna Banka technical-problem coverage. Broadcast coverage of bank incidents is otherwise hard to monitor.
Aggregator with an explicit economy/business stream; its dated article-index URLs suggest a browsable archive useful for backfilling what was published on a given day about banks.
General MK news site with an economy category; adds breadth for cross-checking whether a bank story is single-outlet (possible PR placement) or genuinely picked up.
